title: Tierwise rules file
description: Structure of a rules file, or of one item of inline manifest rules (MANIFEST-16, POL-1, POL-2). A rules file configures exactly one feature, named by 'feature'. It declares its policies, its bindings and optionally its examples. This schema checks structure only. The compiler checks the cross-references and the semantic codes, for example that a setting reference names a setting of the same policy (RULE-22), that a binding names a declared policy (BIND-6), that a root binding exists (BIND-13), that each effect is valid for the feature (FEAT-13), and that every example passes (POL-41, POL-42). Setting references are strings that begin with '$' (RULE-4). Error codes: this schema does not assign codes. Where it rejects a document, the compiler reports the code that the clause cited in the failing definition's description names (for example E_INVALID_SETTING for a setting declaration, E_EFFECT_MISMATCH for an effect, E_INVALID_NODE_ID for a node ID). Where a definition names none, the generic E_INVALID_DECLARATION of FEAT-2 applies. Where the code of a case depends on the feature or on the declared type of a fact (for example the legality of a literal, RULE-17, or of an effect, FEAT-13), the schema accepts the case and the compiler reports it.

feature.description: The name of the feature this rules file configures (POL-2). The compiler reports an unknown name as E_UNKNOWN_FEATURE (POL-3).

policies.description: A map from policy name to policy. The map keys are policy names, and every policy is declared here (POL-6).

propertyNames.description: A policy name. It must be a YAML string.

bindings.description: A map from level name to the bindings written at that level (BIND-1). The root level's entry is one binding with no node ID (BIND-2). Each other level's entry maps node IDs to bindings (BIND-3). The schema cannot tell the root level name, so it accepts either form at each level key. The compiler selects the form from the declared levels and reports a mismatch (BIND-2, BIND-3).

propertyNames.description: A level name, or the root level name. It must be a YAML string.

examples.description: Optional examples of decisions for this feature (POL-28). Each one is run at compile time, and a failing one fails validation (POL-47).

effect.description: An effect. Its validity depends on the feature's 'returns', which this schema cannot see: a string for the enum form, a mapping for the object form (FEAT-7, FEAT-11), or null only when the enum form declares nullable (FEAT-9). The schema therefore places no restriction on the type, and the compiler reports every value that is not valid for the feature, of any type, as E_EFFECT_MISMATCH (FEAT-13, FEAT-14, POL-40). A rule's 'then' must not begin with '$'; the compiler reports that as E_INVALID_SETTING (POL-27).

policy.description: A named, ordered rule list with an optional set of settings and a default effect (POL-7 to POL-9).

default.description: The effect when no rule matches (POL-7, RULE-50).

rules.description: The ordered rule list. The first rule whose conditions all hold is the winner (RULE-46, RULE-47). The list may be empty (POL-8).

settings.description: Optional map from setting name to setting declaration (POL-9). When absent, the policy has no settings.

settingName.description: A setting name. It is non-empty, contains neither '$' nor '.', and is not the reserved name 'policy'. A declaration with another name is reported as E_INVALID_SETTING (POL-20). The compiler NFC-normalises the name before comparison.

setting.description: A named, fact-typed policy parameter. Its value comes from the selected binding, or from 'default' when the binding omits it (BIND-23). It holds exactly one of 'value_of' (one value) or 'list_of' (a list of distinct values) (POL-12). 'default' is required (POL-11) and is never null (POL-18). A setting that is not a mapping is E_INVALID_DECLARATION (FEAT-2). A missing default, both or neither of value_of and list_of, an extra member, a null or mistyped default and an invalid setting name are each reported as E_INVALID_SETTING (POL-11 to POL-13, POL-17, POL-18, POL-20).

default.description: The value used when the selected binding does not set this setting (POL-11). It is a scalar for 'value_of' and a list of scalars for 'list_of'. A null or mistyped default is E_INVALID_SETTING (POL-17, POL-18). A list that repeats an element is reported as E_DUPLICATE_VALUE by the compiler (POL-19), not here.

value_of.description: The fact whose single value this setting holds (POL-12). The fact must be an eligible fact of the decided entity (POL-16).

list_of.description: The fact whose values this setting holds as a list (POL-12). The fact must be an eligible fact of the decided entity (POL-16).

default.description: For 'list_of', the default is a list of scalar values.
For 'value_of', the default is one scalar value.

scalar.description: A scalar YAML value that is not null. A decimal value is a string (TYPE-24, TYPE-25), and an integer is a number.

rule.description: One entry of a policy's rules: an id, a display name, a condition mapping and an effect (POL-21, POL-22). The name is for display and does not affect evaluation (POL-23).

id.description: The rule identifier, unique within its policy (POL-24). It must be a non-empty YAML string, so an integer such as 1 is rejected (POL-25).

name.description: A display name for the rule. It must be a non-empty YAML string (POL-25).

when.description: The conditions of the rule, as a mapping from fact name to condition (RULE-1). The rule matches only when every condition holds (RULE-7). An empty mapping always matches (RULE-2).

then.description: The effect returned when this rule wins (RULE-48). It must be a valid effect for the feature and must not be a setting reference (POL-27).

factName.description: A fact name, written '<entity>.<attribute>' (FACT-1, FACT-3). The schema checks only that it is a string. The compiler checks the form and that the entity and the fact are declared: a name with no '.' (including the empty name) is E_UNKNOWN_ENTITY, and an empty attribute part is E_INVALID_DECLARATION (FACT-3). The attribute may contain '.'.

entityName.description: A child entity name. It must be a YAML string. The compiler checks that it names a child of the decided entity (FACT-29).

conditionMap.description: A mapping from fact name to condition (RULE-1). A fact may appear at most once in one mapping, which YAML enforces (SRC-3).

condition.description: One condition, in one of the four forms of table 8.1 (RULE-3). The 'eq' form is a bare scalar operand, which is either a literal or a setting reference. The other forms use exactly one operator key: 'in' for a single-value fact, 'all_in' or 'any_in' for a child fact. An operand that is a setting reference is a string that begins with '$' (RULE-4). A setting reference must be the whole operand (RULE-23). An operator key outside the table, an operator mapping with no operator key or with more than one, and a list or mapping in the 'eq' form are E_INVALID_DECLARATION (RULE-6). Whether the form fits the fact's kind is checked by the compiler (RULE-13, RULE-14).

oneOf.description: The 'in' form: the fact's value equals one element of the list (RULE-30), or of the list named by a setting reference (RULE-23).

in.description: The operand list of the 'in' form: a literal list (RULE-30) or a reference to a list-valued setting (RULE-23, RULE-24). A single value or null where a list is required is E_INVALID_DECLARATION (RULE-6).

oneOf.description: The 'all_in' form, for a child fact: every child's value is one element of the list (RULE-31). It does not hold on a child collection that is present and empty (RULE-33, FACT-18). An omitted child collection makes the fact missing (FACT-17), so the precheck stops evaluation before the condition is tested (RULE-42).

all_in.description: The operand list of the 'all_in' form: a literal list (RULE-31) or a reference to a list-valued setting (RULE-23, RULE-24). A single value or null where a list is required is E_INVALID_DECLARATION (RULE-6).

oneOf.description: The 'any_in' form, for a child fact: at least one child's value is one element of the list (RULE-32).

any_in.description: The operand list of the 'any_in' form: a literal list (RULE-32) or a reference to a list-valued setting (RULE-23, RULE-24). A single value or null where a list is required is E_INVALID_DECLARATION (RULE-6).

eqOperand.description: The 'eq' form operand: one scalar, or a setting reference when the string begins with '$' (RULE-29, RULE-4). The schema accepts every scalar, including null and a number that is not an integer, because the code depends on the fact's declared type (RULE-17). The compiler reports an illegal literal, including null and a number for a decimal fact, as E_ILLEGAL_FACT_VALUE (RULE-18, RULE-19), and an integer outside the safe range as E_INTEGER_RANGE (RULE-20). A list or a mapping is not valid here and is E_INVALID_DECLARATION (RULE-6).

oneOf.description: A literal list. It may be empty, and an empty list never matches (RULE-34). It must not repeat an element: the compiler reports a repeat as E_DUPLICATE_VALUE (RULE-21).
A setting reference to a list-valued setting (RULE-23, RULE-24).

listOperand.description: The operand of 'in', 'all_in' or 'any_in': a literal list or a setting reference. A single value, null or a mapping is not valid here and is E_INVALID_DECLARATION (RULE-6).

literalList.description: A list of literal values. Each element is a scalar. The compiler reports an illegal element as E_ILLEGAL_FACT_VALUE (RULE-18, RULE-19), and an element that begins with '$' as E_INVALID_SETTING, because a setting reference is not allowed inside a list (RULE-23). A nested list or mapping is not valid and is E_INVALID_DECLARATION (RULE-6).

literal.description: A scalar in a condition list. The schema accepts null, a number that is not an integer and a string that begins with '$', because the codes depend on the fact's declared type and on the position: null and a type-illegal literal are E_ILLEGAL_FACT_VALUE (RULE-18, RULE-19), an integer outside the safe range is E_INTEGER_RANGE (RULE-20), and a '$'-string inside a list is E_INVALID_SETTING (RULE-23).

settingReference.description: A setting reference: a string that begins with '$', followed by the setting name (RULE-4). The compiler checks that the setting exists in the same policy (RULE-22, E_UNKNOWN_SETTING), and has the matching kind and fact (RULE-24, RULE-25, E_INVALID_SETTING).

nodeId.description: A node ID written in a binding or in an example context. The schema checks only that it is a string. The compiler checks that it is non-empty, has at most 128 code points and contains no control character, and reports a failure as E_INVALID_NODE_ID (SCOPE-33, SCOPE-34, SCOPE-38, BIND-10, POL-43). It NFC-normalises the ID (SCOPE-35) and checks catalog membership (SCOPE-43, POL-44).

binding.description: A binding: the selected policy and optional setting values for it (BIND-4). Every entry other than 'policy' names a setting of that policy and gives its value (BIND-8, BIND-9). The schema does not check the entries: whether a name is a setting of the policy (E_UNKNOWN_SETTING, BIND-8) and whether a value is valid (E_INVALID_SETTING, E_DUPLICATE_VALUE, BIND-9, POL-17 to POL-19) depend on the named policy. When the policy is unknown, the entries are not checked at all (BIND-7). A binding that omits a setting takes the setting's default (BIND-23, BIND-24).

policy.description: The name of a policy declared in this rules file (BIND-5). An unknown name is reported as E_UNKNOWN_POLICY (BIND-6). The schema checks only that it is a string.

settingValue.description: A value that a binding gives a setting: a scalar for 'value_of', or a list of scalars for 'list_of' (POL-15, POL-17). The schema places no restriction on it, because the binding's other entries are not checked when its policy is unknown (BIND-7). The compiler reports an invalid value, including null, as E_INVALID_SETTING (POL-17, POL-18), and a repeated list element as E_DUPLICATE_VALUE (POL-19).

nodeBindings.description: The bindings of one non-root level, keyed by node ID (BIND-3). Each node ID is checked by the compiler (BIND-10, E_INVALID_NODE_ID, E_UNKNOWN_NODE).

levelBindings.description: The bindings written at one level. At the root level it is one binding with no node ID (BIND-2). At any other level it is a map of node ID to binding (BIND-3). A binding has a string 'policy' entry, and a node map never has a 'policy' entry whose value is a string, because each node value is a mapping, so the two forms do not overlap. The compiler selects the form from the declared levels and reports a mismatch (BIND-2, BIND-3).

examples.description: A list of examples (POL-28). Each name must be unique within the file (POL-30). An empty list is allowed.

example.description: An example: a context, a FactSet and the effect that the decision is expected to return (POL-28). An example uses the shorthand form when it has no 'children', and then a list value under 'facts' is shorthand for child maps (POL-32, POL-33). An example with 'children' uses the explicit form, and then no list is allowed under 'facts' (POL-32, POL-45).

name.description: The example's name, which identifies it in findings (POL-29). Names must be unique within the file (POL-30).

context.description: The context for the decision: a map with optional 'levels' and 'axes' members (POL-28, POL-31). It must not name the root level (CTX-3). A shape error is E_INVALID_DECLARATION (POL-43).

facts.description: The single-value facts of the FactSet (FACT-23, FACT-24). In the shorthand form, a list value here is a child fact written as shorthand (POL-33). A fact whose value is null is missing (FACT-16).

children.description: The explicit child maps of the FactSet, keyed by child entity (FACT-14, FACT-29). Its presence selects the explicit form (POL-32).

expect.description: The effect that the decide operation must return for this example (POL-40, POL-41). An invalid value is E_EFFECT_MISMATCH (POL-40).

facts.description: When the example has children, its facts must have no list values.

additionalProperties.description: In the explicit form, no list value is allowed under 'facts' (POL-32, POL-45).

context.description: The context of an example: an optional map of level names to node IDs and an optional map of axis names to node IDs (POL-31, CTX-1, CTX-2). It may hold no other member, and a map of the wrong shape is not valid: the compiler reports either as E_INVALID_DECLARATION (POL-43). It may not name the root level, which is also E_INVALID_DECLARATION (CTX-3, POL-43). An undeclared level or axis is E_UNKNOWN_SCOPE and a malformed node ID is E_INVALID_NODE_ID (POL-43); a node ID outside a closed catalog is E_UNKNOWN_NODE (POL-44). At runtime the same faults are E_CONTEXT_INVALID (CTX-2, CTX-3).

levels.description: A map from non-root level name to node ID.

axes.description: A map from axis name to node ID.

nodeMap.description: A map from scope name to node ID. Each value must be a string (CTX-1); another type is E_INVALID_DECLARATION (POL-43).

propertyNames.description: A level or axis name. It must be a YAML string.

facts.description: The single-value facts of an example's FactSet, keyed by fact name (FACT-23, FACT-26). A null value is a missing fact (FACT-16). A list value is valid only as shorthand, and only when the example has no 'children' (POL-33, POL-37).

factValue.description: A fact value in a FactSet: a scalar, null for a missing fact (FACT-16, POL-39), or, as shorthand, a list of scalars for a child fact (POL-33). A null element of a shorthand list is a child map with a missing fact (FACT-19, FACT-35). A mapping is not a fact value; the compiler reports it as E_ILLEGAL_FACT_VALUE (POL-39). Whether a scalar fits the fact's declared type is checked by the compiler (POL-39).

items.description: One element of a shorthand list: a scalar or null.

children.description: The child collections of a FactSet, keyed by child entity name (FACT-14). Each collection is a list of child maps (FACT-31, FACT-32). An empty list is a child collection that is present and empty (FACT-18).

additionalProperties.description: A list of child maps, one for each child element.

childMap.description: One child map: the child facts of one child element, keyed by fact name (FACT-14, FACT-33). Each value is a scalar or null, and a null value is a missing fact (FACT-19).

additionalProperties.description: A child fact value: a scalar, or null for a missing fact.
